title: Building a Password System From Scratch
core_premise: Every naive way of storing passwords breaks under real attacks until you combine one-way hashing, random salts, and intentionally slow memory-hard math.
persistent_subject: One persistent login pipeline connecting a User Node, Hash Engine, and Users Database Table that upgrades from v1.0 to v4.0.

voice.style_prompt: Crisp, fast-paced tech explainer with sharp contrast when systems break and lock back down.

beats.narration: How do apps actually keep your password safe from hackers?
beats.visual_state: Dark blueprint canvas showing a User Node connected to an empty Database cylinder with a glowing lock outline.
beats.visual_diff: Reveal core Login Client -> Server -> Database silhouette and hook question.

beats.narration: Step one: save every user's raw password straight into a simple database table.
beats.visual_state: v1.0 pipeline sends visible text 'hunter2' straight into a clean two-column Users Table (email, password).
beats.visual_diff: Populate database table rows with readable plaintext passwords.

beats.narration: One leaked backup or SQL injection exposes every single password in readable English instantly.
beats.visual_state: Red breach beam splits the v1.0 Users Table open, spilling readable passwords across the screen under an ALL LEAKED stamp.
beats.visual_diff: Trigger SQL injection breach beam, red screen vignette, and ALL LEAKED stamp.
beats.stress_test_trigger: SQL injection dumps the entire users table

beats.narration: Fix one: run passwords through a one-way SHA-256 hash so you cannot reverse them.
beats.visual_state: A cyan SHA-256 shredder node sits before the Users Table, turning 'hunter2' into a fixed 64-char fingerprint.
beats.visual_diff: Insert one-way SHA-256 hash module between login input and Users Table.

beats.narration: Identical passwords create identical hashes. Attackers match stolen hashes against precomputed cheat-sheet tables in milliseconds.
beats.visual_state: Two users share the exact same hash string, lighting up a matching row inside an attacker's Rainbow Table lookup panel.
beats.visual_diff: Overlay precomputed Rainbow Table matching duplicate user hashes instantaneously.
beats.stress_test_trigger: Attacker queries a precomputed rainbow table of 10B common hashes

beats.narration: Fix two: attach a unique random salt to each user before hashing, destroying cheat-sheets.
beats.visual_state: A Random Salt dice node injects distinct random prefixes into identical passwords, producing completely different hashes in the table.
beats.visual_diff: Add per-user Random Salt injector before SHA-256 node, scrambling identical hashes.

beats.narration: Because SHA-256 is built for speed, modern GPU clusters still guess billions of salted passwords every second.
beats.visual_state: A glowing GPU rack fires high-speed guess beams through salted hashes, pushing the Guess Rate meter into red overload.
beats.visual_diff: Connect attacker GPU cluster flooding SHA-256 at 100B guesses/sec.
beats.stress_test_trigger: GPU cluster brute-forcing 100 billion salted hashes per second

beats.narration: Fix three: switch to Argon2. It intentionally burns time and memory, making every guess painfully expensive.
beats.visual_state: The fast SHA-256 chip swaps to a heavy Argon2 memory-block throttle; incoming GPU guess beams bottleneck to a crawl.
beats.visual_diff: Replace SHA-256 with memory-hard Argon2 throttle blocking GPU throughput.

beats.narration: Plaintext to salted Argon2: real security isn't hiding secrets, it's making stolen math unaffordable to crack.
beats.visual_state: Complete v4.0 pipeline glows green across User -> Random Salt -> Argon2 -> Users Table with resilient shields locked.
beats.visual_diff: Zoom out to full v4.0 progression ribbon (v1 -> v4) and lock final takeaway card.
